biography.plain_text: Titouan Lamazou is a painter, author and navigator. He won the inaugural Vendée Globe in 1990, completing the solo, nonstop circumnavigation in just over 109 days, and won the Route du Rhum that year. He then made art his central profession, producing travel books, portraits, photography and museum exhibitions shaped by journeys across five continents.

long_biography.plain_text:
Winning the first Vendée Globe ended Titouan Lamazou's desire to be a champion rather than intensifying it. He had entered offshore racing to test himself, finished second in the BOC Challenge and pursued the new solo circumnavigation with single-minded determination. Once across the finish line, he announced his withdrawal from ocean racing and returned to the artistic vocation he had chosen as a child.

Travel remained his method, but observation replaced competition. For six years Lamazou crossed five continents to portray women, combining painting, photography and testimony in Femmes du Monde. What began as a celebration of individual lives became an argument against misogyny and earned recognition as a UNESCO Artist for Peace. His newer Pacific work turns the same attentive practice towards islands, ocean cultures and the preservation of living systems.
